final_proof:
As written, the explanatory type declarations contain two errors, so the claimed composite is not literally well-typed. If \(L:\mathbf D\to\mathbf C\), then the opposite functor has type \(L^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\), not \(\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\). Also, the ordinary hom bifunctor of \(\mathbf C\) has type
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-):\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\longrightarrow\mathbf{Set},
\]
not \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\to\mathbf{Set}\). With these necessary corrections, the statement is
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-)\circ (L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C})
\]
as functors \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\to\mathbf{Set}\). We prove this equality.

Because \(\mathbf C\) is locally small, every hom-class used below is a set. For an object \((D,X)\) of \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\), the right-hand side has value
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(-,-)\circ(L^{\mathrm{op}}\times\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}))(D,X)
&=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(LD,X).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is exactly the value of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)\) at \((D,X)\).

It remains to compare the action on morphisms. Let
\[
(u,v):(D,X)\longrightarrow(D',X')
\]
be a morphism of \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathbf C\). Thus \(v:X\to X'\) is a morphism in \(\mathbf C\), while \(u:D\to D'\) in \(\mathbf D^{\mathrm{op}}\) corresponds to a morphism \(\bar u:D'\to D\) in \(\mathbf D\). The morphism \(L^{\mathrm{op}}u:LD\to LD'\) in \(\mathbf C^{\mathrm{op}}\) corresponds in \(\mathbf C\) to
\[
L\bar u:LD'\longrightarrow LD.
\]
By the definition of the hom bifunctor, the right-hand side therefore sends a member \(h:LD\to X\) of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(LD,X)\) to
\[
v\circ h\circ L\bar u:LD'\longrightarrow X'.
\]
But this is precisely the definition of the action of the hom bifunctor with left functor \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C}(L-,-)\) on \((u,v)\): it is contravariant in the \(\mathbf D\)-variable through \(L\), and covariant in the \(\mathbf C\)-variable. Hence the two functors agree on every object and every morphism. Consequently they are equal (with the standard objectwise and morphismwise definitions of these functors), proving the corrected claim.
